header.userPrompt:
Consolidate the Telegram receipt flow into a single bot message per receipt that is edited in place through its lifecycle, with stage text so the user sees that work is happening, and richer details on the ready/created states. Backend only (the Telegram bot), no frontend.

## Problem today (read these first)
A single receipt currently produces three separate Telegram messages, and the "Create Expense" button never goes away:
- `server/.../actions/telegram/TelegramPhotoAction.scala:57` sends a plain "Receipt saved ✓" message (its id is never kept).
- `server/.../actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala:116-121` sends a second message with a "Create Expense" web-app button and DISCARDS the returned message id (`.map(_ => ())`).
- `server/.../actions/telegram/UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.scala:144-170` (`notifyTelegram`) runs when the expense is created in the mini app: because no message id was stored, `expenseMessageId` is `None`, so it sends a THIRD message with an "Edit" web-app button and stores that id; later edits edit that third message's text.
Result: the Create button message is never updated or removed, so it lingers forever, and the user gets a disconnected trail of messages.

The data model already supports one message: `server/.../repositories/models/TelegramReceipt.scala` has `chatId` and `expenseMessageId: Option[Long]`, and `TelegramReceiptRepository` has `create(id, receiptId, chatId)`, `findByReceiptId`, `findByExpenseId`, `updateExpenseMessageId(id, messageId)`. Reuse the existing `expense_message_id` column as the single bot-message id for the receipt; do NOT rename it and do NOT add an evolution.

## Telegram API helpers (`server/.../apis/TelegramApi.scala`)
Currently: `sendMessage(chatId, text): Future[Unit]`, `sendMessageWithWebAppButton(chatId, text, webAppUrl, buttonLabel): Future[Long]` (returns the message id), `editMessage(chatId, messageId, text): Future[Unit]` (EditMessageText, text only, no reply markup).

Add the two primitives the single-message flow needs, following the existing style and the bot4s models already imported:
1. A way to send the initial message and get its id back. Either a `sendMessage` variant returning `Future[Long]`, or reuse `sendMessageWithWebAppButton` where a button is wanted. Do not change the signature of the existing `Unit`-returning `sendMessage` (it has unrelated callers: `TelegramLinkAction`, `TelegramHandleTextAction`, the unlinked-user notice); add a new method instead.
2. Extend editing so it can set BOTH text and the button (so a stage edit can swap Create -> Edit -> no button). `EditMessageText` accepts `replyMarkup`; add an `editMessage` overload/variant taking an optional web-app button (label + url), or `None` for no button. Keep the existing text-only `editMessage` or fold callers into the new one, your choice, but every stage edit must be able to set the correct button.

Handle Telegram's "message is not modified" response gracefully (treat as success, do not error) and keep edits resilient: if an edit fails because the user deleted the message, fall back to sending a fresh message with the right button and store the new id (generalize the recover-and-resend pattern already in `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction`).

## Target lifecycle: one message, edited in place
Store the message id once, at photo time, then every later stage EDITS that id instead of sending a new message.

1. Received (synchronous, in `TelegramPhotoAction`): right after the telegram_receipt row exists, send an initial status message (no button) such as "Receipt received, analyzing..." using the id-returning method, and store its id via `updateExpenseMessageId`. Replace the current "Receipt saved ✓" send. This immediate ack is important: it is the only update that happens before the background jobs run. If a telegram_receipt already exists for this receipt (duplicate photo, deduped by sha256 in `uploadReceipt`), reuse/edit its existing message rather than creating another row or message; keep this minimal.
2. Classifying/reading (in `ProcessDocumentAction`): when classification completes and the document is a receipt heading into parsing, edit the stored message to a stage text such as "Reading the receipt...". When it is rejected as not a ticket (the `notATicketMessage` branch at `ProcessDocumentAction.scala:78` and `ParseReceiptAction.scala:164`), edit the stored message to that failure text with NO button, instead of sending a new message via the notifier.
3. Ready (in `ParseReceiptAction`): when parsing succeeds, EDIT the stored message to a summary plus the "Create Expense" web-app button (same `webAppUrl` as today), instead of sending a new message. Put richer detail in this summary from the parsed data available here: vendor/merchant name, total, date, and item count when available. On terminal parse failure (the existing `Left(UnsupportedKind)` / `Left(ParseError)` branches), edit the stored message to the failure text with no button. Do NOT show a failure state for a transient/retriable exception that bubbles up for job retry; only the existing terminal `Left` branches map to a failure edit.
4. Created / edited (in `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.notifyTelegram`): edit the stored message to the saved-expense details plus the "Edit" web-app button, swapping the button from Create to Edit. Because the id is now stored from photo time, this path edits the same single message every time (including repeated edits). Keep the deleted-message fallback.

Stage texts are plain and discrete. Do NOT animate a spinner or edit on a timer (Telegram rate-limits edits to about one per second per chat, and an animation adds noise with no information). A static summary per stage is enough. Avoid em-dashes and en-dashes in all message strings (use plain punctuation; the existing middot `·` and `✓` are fine).

## Keep identical / out of scope
- Unrelated Telegram messages (`/link` replies, the text handler, the unlinked-user notice) stay as plain sends.
- No new inline callback buttons / discard action, no change to the mini app or any frontend, no dedup integration, no DB evolution, no change to how documents are parsed or classified beyond where the message is edited.
- Do not change the background-job framework, retry, or visibility-timeout behavior.

## Rules and constraints
- No silent bad data; fail loudly where the code already does; never fabricate parsed values.
- When a call passes two or more arguments of the same type (e.g. `editMessage(chatId: Long, messageId: Long, ...)` which has two `Long`s), pass them by name (a reviewer enforces this).
- Telegram send/edit failures must never break the pipeline: they are logged and recovered, exactly as the current notifier/upsert code already does.
- Follow `docs/guide/backend.md` and `docs/guide/testing.md`. Test descriptions name a single method, per `.orca/reviewers/tests.md`. Tests must not hit the real Telegram API: use a fake `TelegramApi` (mirror whatever fake/stub the existing Telegram action tests use) that records sent and edited messages.
- Match existing code style; surgical changes only; every changed line traces to this request.

## Tests
Add/extend tests for the single-message behavior using a fake `TelegramApi` that records calls:
- photo receipt sends exactly one initial message and stores its id on the telegram_receipt;
- parse-ready EDITS that same stored id and attaches the Create Expense button (no new message sent);
- not-a-ticket and terminal parse-failure EDIT the stored id to a failure text with no button (no new message);
- create via the web app EDITS the same stored id and swaps to the Edit button; a subsequent edit edits the same id again;
- unrelated sends (link/text) are unchanged.
Follow the existing Telegram action test patterns and `test-isolation` (random unique data). The full suite must pass as CI runs it.

resultJson.description:
Today one Telegram receipt produces three separate bot messages: "Receipt saved ✓" at photo time, a "Create Expense" web-app button message after parsing (its id is thrown away), and a third "Expense saved" message with an "Edit" button once the expense is created in the mini app. The Create button never goes away, and the user is left with a trail of disconnected messages. This epic merges them into ONE bot message per receipt. It is sent at photo time, its id goes into the existing `telegram_receipt.expense_message_id` column (no rename, no evolution), and every later pipeline stage edits that message in place. The stages are: Received ("Receipt received, analyzing...") -> Reading ("Reading the receipt...") -> Ready (summary with vendor, total, date and item count, plus the Create Expense button) or a terminal failure text with no button -> Created/Edited (saved-expense details with the Edit button). Repeated edits always target the same id.

Mechanically, TelegramApi gains an id-returning send and an edit that can set or clear a web-app button. Edit treats Telegram's "message is not modified" as success. One shared helper in DocumentTelegramNotifier implements "show this text/button on the receipt's message": it edits the stored id, or sends a fresh message and stores its id when there is no stored id or the edit fails (for example, the user deleted the message). It never fails the caller. Every stage (photo, ProcessDocumentAction, ParseReceiptAction, UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction) goes through that helper or the new TelegramApi primitives. Telegram failures are only logged, as today. Unrelated sends (/link replies, text handler, unlinked-user notice) stay plain `sendMessage`. Stage texts are static: no spinner or timer edits, and no em/en dashes (`·` and `✓` are fine).

Decisions taken where the spec was ambiguous: (1) A duplicate photo (sha256 dedupe finds an existing receipt that already has a telegram_receipt row) creates no new row, sends no new message and edits nothing; the existing message already shows that receipt's current stage, and no new job runs for it. (2) In ParseReceiptAction the post-Textract advisory "not a ticket" hint does not stop parsing; the document still reaches Ready a few milliseconds later. A separate edit would be overwritten at once and risks Telegram's per-chat edit rate limit. So that hint is folded in as the first line of the Ready summary instead of being its own no-button edit. The ProcessDocumentAction pre-Textract rejection IS terminal and edits to the failure text with no button. (3) Retriable exceptions that bubble up for job retry never produce a failure edit; only the existing terminal `Left`/no-cache branches do.

tasks.title: TelegramApi: id-returning send, button-aware edit, and a shared FakeTelegramApi test double
tasks.description:
In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/TelegramApi.scala`:
- Add `final case class WebAppButton(label: String, url: String)` in a `TelegramApi` companion object.
- Add `sendMessageReturningId(chatId: Long, text: String, button: Option[TelegramApi.WebAppButton]): Future[Long]`. It is a `SendMessage` with `replyMarkup = button.map(b => InlineKeyboardMarkup.singleButton(InlineKeyboardButton(text = b.label, webApp = Some(WebAppInfo(b.url)))))` and returns `_.messageId.toLong`.
- Add the overload `editMessage(chatId: Long, messageId: Long, text: String, button: Option[TelegramApi.WebAppButton]): Future[Unit]`, using `EditMessageText(..., replyMarkup = <same markup or None>)`. Sending `None` must remove an existing keyboard. If bot4s omits a None replyMarkup from the JSON, pass `Some(InlineKeyboardMarkup(Seq.empty))` so Telegram clears the button, and check that in the spec.
- In the new edit only, recover a Telegram error whose description contains "message is not modified" as success.
- Leave the existing `sendMessage(chatId, text): Future[Unit]`, `sendMessageWithWebAppButton` and the text-only `editMessage` untouched; later tasks remove them once they are orphaned.

Tests, in `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/TelegramApiSpec.scala`, reusing its `FakeRequestHandler`:
- `sendMessageReturningId` returns the id, attaches the button markup, and sends no markup when the button is None.
- `editMessage` with a button sets the web-app markup; with None it clears or omits it.
- `editMessage` completes successfully when the handler fails with a "Bad Request: message is not modified" Telegram exception, and fails for any other error.
The handler may need a failing variant.

Also add `server/src/test/scala/utils/FakeTelegramApi.scala`. It is a recording fake that extends `TelegramApi` with placeholder `TelegramConfig(enabled = false, ...)` and `new DefaultApplicationLifecycle`, like `RepositoryUtils.documentTelegramNotifier`. It overrides `sendMessage`, `sendMessageReturningId`, `editMessage` (both overloads), `sendMessageWithWebAppButton` and `downloadFile`, recording calls in thread-safe buffers, for example `sent: Seq[Sent(chatId, text, button)]` and `edited: Seq[Edited(chatId, messageId, text, button)]`. Each send returns a fresh id from an AtomicLong. Optional knobs: a canned `downloadFile` result, and making edits fail, to simulate a deleted message. No network calls.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *TelegramApiSpec"`.

tasks.title: DocumentTelegramNotifier: single-message show helper with deleted-message fallback; drop em-dashes
tasks.description:
In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/services/DocumentTelegramNotifier.scala`, add the shared single-message primitive:
- `showOnReceiptMessage(telegramReceipt: TelegramReceipt, userId: UUID, text: String, button: Option[TelegramApi.WebAppButton]): Future[Unit]`. When `expenseMessageId` is `Some(id)`, call `telegramApi.editMessage(chatId = ..., messageId = id, text = ..., button = ...)` with named args (two Longs). If the edit fails, `recoverWith`: send a fresh message with the same text and button via `sendMessageReturningId` and store its id with `telegramReceiptRepository.updateExpenseMessageId(id = telegramReceipt.telegramReceiptId, messageId = newId)`. When `expenseMessageId` is `None` (photo-time send failed, or a legacy row), send fresh and store the id the same way. The method never fails: an outer `.recover` logs a warning with `userId=` and the receipt id.
- `updateReceiptMessage(documentId: UUID, userId: UUID, text: String, button: Option[TelegramApi.WebAppButton]): Future[Unit]` resolves receipt -> telegram_receipt like `notify` does, logs and no-ops when either is missing, then delegates to `showOnReceiptMessage`.
- Keep the existing `notify` for now; the ParseReceiptAction task removes it once orphaned.
- Rewrite `notATicketMessage` without em-dashes, e.g. "This doesn't look like a purchase ticket. Please send the itemized ticket." and "This looks like ${other.withArticle}, not a purchase ticket. Please send the itemized ticket." Existing tests reference the function, not the literal, so they keep compiling.

Add `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/services/DocumentTelegramNotifierSpec.scala`. It is a `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils` using real repositories and `utils.FakeTelegramApi`, with random data via `createUser()`/`createReceipt()` plus `repositories.telegramReceipt.create`/`updateExpenseMessageId`. Cover:
- `showOnReceiptMessage` edits the stored id with the given button and sends nothing.
- When the edit fails, it sends one fresh message with the button and stores the new id.
- With no stored id, it sends and stores.
- `updateReceiptMessage` is a no-op with no Telegram calls when the receipt has no telegram_receipt.
- It never fails when Telegram fails entirely.
Test descriptions name only the method.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *DocumentTelegramNotifierSpec"`.

tasks.title: TelegramPhotoAction: send and store the single initial status message
tasks.description:
In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/telegram/TelegramPhotoAction.scala`, replace the `sendMessage(chatId, "Receipt saved ✓")` step:
- When `findByReceiptId(receiptId)` is `None`: generate the telegram_receipt id, `create(...)` the row, then `telegramApi.sendMessageReturningId(chatId, "Receipt received, analyzing...", None)` and `telegramReceiptRepository.updateExpenseMessageId(id = trId, messageId = msgId)` (named args). Wrap the send+store in `.recover` that logs a warning with `userId=`. A Telegram failure must not fail the webhook, and later stages fall back to sending fresh when no id is stored.
- When it is `Some(_)` (duplicate photo deduped by sha256): no new row, no message, no edit; log at info with userId and receiptId.
- The unlinked-user notice stays a plain `sendMessage`.

Update `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/telegram/TelegramPhotoActionSpec.scala` to use `utils.FakeTelegramApi` instead of the Mockito stub, with a canned `downloadFile`. Cover these `apply` cases:
- Sends exactly one initial message with no button and stores its id on the telegram_receipt (`findByReceiptId(...).value.expenseMessageId` equals the recorded id).
- Sending the same photo twice keeps one row and one sent message, and makes no edits.
- The unlinked user gets the unchanged plain notice and no download.
- No expense is created.
- A failing initial send still completes and leaves `expenseMessageId` empty.
Use `RandomData.randomTelegramUserId()`.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *TelegramPhotoActionSpec"`.

tasks.title: ProcessDocumentAction: edit to 'Reading the receipt...' and to the not-a-ticket failure
tasks.description:
In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/documents/ProcessDocumentAction.scala` `gateThenAnalyze`:
- In the rejection branch, replace `notifier.notify(doc.id, doc.userId, DocumentTelegramNotifier.notATicketMessage(rejected))` with `notifier.updateReceiptMessage(doc.id, doc.userId, DocumentTelegramNotifier.notATicketMessage(rejected), None)`. Use named args for the two UUIDs.
- In the `case None` branch, call `notifier.updateReceiptMessage(..., "Reading the receipt...", None)` before `analyze(doc, receipt)`, sequenced in the for-comprehension.
- The notifier never fails, so job retry/visibility behaviour is unchanged. A retried job re-sends the same text, which the API treats as "not modified" success.

Extend `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/documents/ProcessDocumentActionSpec.scala`. Build the action with `new DocumentTelegramNotifier(repositories.receipts, repositories.telegramReceipt, fakeApi)` using `utils.FakeTelegramApi`; the existing tests keep `documentTelegramNotifier`. Set up via `createReceipt(user.id)`, `repositories.telegramReceipt.create` + `updateExpenseMessageId`, and a stored classification via `repositories.documents.updateClassification`, so `classify` uses `fromStored` and no JEV is called. Cases:
- Stored `BankVoucher` with high confidence: the receipt becomes Unsupported and the stored message id is edited to `notATicketMessage(BankVoucher)` with no button; nothing is sent.
- Stored `PurchaseTicket` and a Textract cache row for the doc's sha256 (`repositories.textractCache.create`), so the cache-hit path never touches `FailingTextractClient`: the stored id is edited to "Reading the receipt..." with no button, and nothing is sent.
Check `DocumentClassifier.fromStored`/`rejection` for the confidence needed to reject.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *ProcessDocumentActionSpec"`.

tasks.title: ParseReceiptAction: Ready edit with richer summary + Create button; terminal failures edit with no button
tasks.description:
In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala`:

Ready:
- Replace the `sendMessageWithWebAppButton(..., "Create Expense").map(_ => ())` block with `notifier.updateReceiptMessage(..., summary, Some(TelegramApi.WebAppButton("Create Expense", s"${webAppConfig.host}/api/telegram/webapp?receipt=${receipt.id}")))`.
- Build the summary from the parsed data only, with no fabricated values. It joins with " · " the vendor (`parsed.vendor_name`, non-empty), the total (`parsed.amount`, plus `parsed.currency` if present), the date (the already-validated `date: Option[LocalDate]`), and "N items" (when `parsed.line_items.nonEmpty`, using the singular for 1). An example is "Receipt ready: Starbucks · 12.34 · 2026-01-15 · 3 items". With no fields it is "Receipt ready." Keep this as a small private pure function.

Advisory hint:
- Change `classifyAfterTextract` to return `Future[Option[String]]`: the `notATicketMessage(cls)` hint instead of calling `notifier.notify`, and `None` on skip or on the existing fail-open recover.
- Pass the hint into the success path so the Ready text starts with it as a first line, separated by a newline. Don't send a separate edit.
- Unsupported/ParseError branches ignore the hint.

Terminal failures:
- Rewrite `notifyTelegramError` (or inline it) to `notifier.updateReceiptMessage(doc.id, receipt.userId, text, None)` for the existing no-cache, `UnsupportedKind` and `ParseError` branches, keeping the existing texts.
- Do not add any failure edit for exceptions that propagate for retry.

Remove orphans this change creates: the `telegramApi` and `telegramReceiptRepository` constructor params if unused, and `DocumentTelegramNotifier.notify` once no caller remains (ProcessDocumentAction has already moved off it; check with Grep).

Tests:
- Update `ParseReceiptActionSpec` and `ParseReceiptActionStatusSpec` constructors.
- Rewrite the Telegram assertions in `ParseReceiptActionSpec` to work through `utils.FakeTelegramApi` and a notifier. Its repos are mocks, so stub `telegramReceiptRepo.findByReceiptId` with a `TelegramReceipt` whose `expenseMessageId = Some(id)`. Alternatively, move the Telegram-facing cases into `ParseReceiptActionStatusSpec` with real repos; that is preferred per the tests reviewer (fakes/real over mocks).
- Cover:
  - Parse success edits the stored id with the Create Expense button and the expected summary (vendor/total/date/items), and sends nothing new.
  - Missing optional fields are simply omitted.
  - The advisory hint appears as the first line of the Ready text with the Create button.
  - Unsupported kind, missing Textract cache and ParseError each edit the stored id to their failure text with no button and send nothing.
  - No telegram_receipt means no Telegram calls.
- Keep the classification tests' existing intent and replace `sendMessage` verifications.
- JSON fixtures must be multi-line.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *ParseReceiptAction*"`.

tasks.title: UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction: edit the same message with saved details and the Edit button
tasks.description:
In `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/telegram/UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.scala`, rewrite `notifyTelegram`:
- After `telegramReceiptRepository.findByExpenseId(expenseId)` returns `Some(tr)`, delegate to `notifier.showOnReceiptMessage(tr, userId, text, Some(TelegramApi.WebAppButton("Edit", s"${webAppConfig.host}/api/telegram/webapp?expense=$expenseId")))`. Inject `DocumentTelegramNotifier`. Its edit-or-send-and-store logic replaces the hand-rolled None/Some + recoverWith code, and the stored photo-time id means create and every later edit hit the same message.
- Keep the outer `.recover` log. Add `userId=` to it, since `userId` is in scope; pass `userId` through.
- Text: keep "Expense saved: $merchantName · $amount · $date" and append " · $category" when a category was given. The richer created state uses only data the action already has, with no dashes.

Remove orphans: `telegramApi` from the constructor if now unused, and then `TelegramApi.sendMessageWithWebAppButton` and the text-only `editMessage` if no callers remain (Grep main and test; also delete their `TelegramApiSpec` cases). Guice wiring is automatic, and no controller spec binds `TelegramApi`.

Update `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseActionSpec`. Its constructor changes. For the Telegram cases, use a real `DocumentTelegramNotifier` over `utils.FakeTelegramApi`; the repos may stay mocked if you stub `findByExpenseId`/`updateExpenseMessageId`. Cover:
- Create edits the stored id (from photo time) with the Edit button and the expected text, and sends nothing.
- A subsequent update edits the same id again.
- An edit failure (deleted message) sends one fresh message with the Edit button and stores the new id.
- A row with no stored id sends and stores.
- The action returns Right even when Telegram or the lookup fails.
- Validation cases are unchanged.

Also confirm unrelated sends are untouched: `TelegramLinkAction`, `TelegramHandleTextAction` and the unlinked notice still call plain `sendMessage`, and their existing specs (e.g. `TelegramExpenseActionSpec`) pass. Run `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "testOnly *Telegram* *ParseReceiptAction* *ProcessDocumentAction* *DocumentTelegramNotifier*"`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- server/ (Play, Scala 3): actions -> repositories (Anorm). Telegram bot code lives in `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/{apis,actions/telegram,actions/documents,services,repositories}`. Backend only; no frontend, lib/api or evolution changes.

KEY FILES
- `apis/TelegramApi.scala`: class `TelegramApi @Inject()(telegramConfig: TelegramConfig, lifecycle: ApplicationLifecycle)(implicit ec)` extends bot4s `TelegramBot` (bot4s telegram-core_3 7.0.0). Current methods:
  - `sendMessage(chatId: Long, text: String): Future[Unit]` (keep; used by TelegramLinkAction, TelegramHandleTextAction, the unlinked notice)
  - `sendMessageWithWebAppButton(chatId, text, webAppUrl, buttonLabel): Future[Long]`
  - `editMessage(chatId: Long, messageId: Long, text: String): Future[Unit]` (EditMessageText; `messageId.toInt`)
  - `downloadFile(fileId): Future[(Array[Byte], String)]`
  Buttons: `InlineKeyboardMarkup.singleButton(InlineKeyboardButton(text = label, webApp = Some(WebAppInfo(url))))`. A custom `given Decoder[Either[Boolean, Message]]` exists for EditMessageText's response. Telegram API errors surface from `request(...)` as bot4s `TelegramApiException` (believed `com.bot4s.telegram.api.TelegramApiException(message, errorCode, cause, parameters)`; verify the package compiles). The "not modified" error description contains "message is not modified".
- `actions/telegram/TelegramPhotoAction.scala`: webhook photo handler. `uploadReceipt` dedupes by sha256 (an existing doc returns the existing receiptId and enqueues no new job). It then creates a telegram_receipt if absent, then sends "Receipt saved ✓" (line 57, to replace).
- `actions/documents/ProcessDocumentAction.scala`: background job. `gateThenAnalyze`: the classifier rejection branch (line ~78, terminal: sets Unsupported, uses `notifier.notify`), otherwise `analyze` (sets Processing; on a Textract cache hit it enqueues ParseReceipt immediately, otherwise starts Textract + PollReceipt in 5s). It does not inject TelegramApi; it uses `DocumentTelegramNotifier`.
- `actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala`: background job. Constructor: (documentsRepository, receiptRepository, merchantsRepository, ruleRepository, textractCacheRepository, telegramReceiptRepository, telegramApi, webAppConfig, documentClassifier, notifier).
  - No cache: Unsupported + error text.
  - `DocumentParser.parse` returns `Right(parsed)`, `Left(UnsupportedKind)` or `Left(ParseError)`.
  - `classifyAfterTextract` is an advisory, fail-open post-Textract classification that currently calls `notifier.notify` but parsing continues.
  - The success path sends the Create Expense button (lines 111-125) with URL `${webAppConfig.host}/api/telegram/webapp?receipt=${receipt.id}`.
  - `notifyTelegramError` uses plain sendMessage.
  - `parsed: DocumentParser.ParsedData` fields: vendor_name, tax_id, transaction_date (String), transaction_time, ticket_id, amount: Option[BigDecimal], currency, fx_rate, base_amount, subtotal, tax_amount, ticket_subtype, line_items: List[LineItem]. A validated `date: Option[LocalDate]` is computed in the action.
- `actions/telegram/UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.scala`: mini-app create/update. `notifyTelegram(expenseId, merchantName, amount, date)` finds the telegram_receipt by expense id; None id -> send Edit button + store; Some -> text-only edit, recoverWith send + store. Edit URL is `${webAppConfig.host}/api/telegram/webapp?expense=$expenseId`. `userId` and `category: Option[String]` are in scope in `apply`.
- `services/DocumentTelegramNotifier.scala`: `@Inject()(receiptRepository, telegramReceiptRepository, telegramApi)(implicit ec)`. `notify(documentId, userId, text)` resolves receipt -> telegram_receipt -> plain send, logs and recovers. Companion `notATicketMessage(documentClass)` currently contains em-dashes.
- `repositories/TelegramReceiptRepository.scala`: `create(id: UUID, receiptId: UUID, chatId: Long): Future[Unit]`, `findByReceiptId(receiptId)`, `findByExpenseId(expenseId)`, `updateExpenseMessageId(id: UUID, messageId: Long)` (`id` is the telegram_receipt id). Model `repositories/models/TelegramReceipt(telegramReceiptId: UUID, receiptId: UUID, chatId: Long, expenseMessageId: Option[Long], createdAt, updatedAt)`. `expense_message_id` is reused as THE single bot-message id; do not rename it and add no evolution.

CONVENTIONS
- Telegram failures never break the pipeline or webhook: `.recover { case e => logger.warn(...) }` as existing code does. Log with `userId=$userId` when a user is in scope.
- Never drop a Future; sequence it in the for-comprehension.
- Pass same-typed args by name: e.g. `editMessage(chatId = c, messageId = m, ...)` (two Longs), `updateExpenseMessageId(id = ..., messageId = ...)`, and calls with two UUIDs such as `(documentId, userId)`. Named args are always allowed.
- No silent defaults or fabricated parsed values: omit missing fields from summaries.
- Message strings contain no em/en dashes; `·` and `✓` are OK. Stage texts are static, with no timers or spinners.
- Comments explain intent, never history ("now", "previously", "instead of").
- Remove only orphans your change creates; surgical diffs; match the existing style. Run scalafmt (`sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`) before finishing.

TESTING
- Server specs: `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils` gives real docker Postgres via `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, plus helpers in `server/src/test/scala/utils/RepositoryUtils.scala`:
  - `createUser()` (random email)
  - `createReceipt(userId)`, which creates a document with unique sha `"sha-"+docId` + receipt + ProcessDocument job and returns `Receipt.Create` (has `.id`, `.documentId`)
  - `createDocument(...)` (default sha "abc123", which is unique per user only)
  - `mockDocumentClassifier`, `noOpBlobStorage`, `documentTelegramNotifier` (built on a real, disabled TelegramApi that must never be called)
  - Repos: `repositories.telegramReceipt`, `.receipts`, `.documents` (`updateClassification(docId, userId, DocumentClassification)`), `.textractCache` (`create(TextractCache.Create)`), `.telegram` (`createBotUser`).
  - `RandomData.randomTelegramUserId()` and friends.
- Unit specs (e.g. `ParseReceiptActionSpec`, `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseActionSpec`) use AnyWordSpec + Mockito repo mocks and `mock[TelegramApi]`. Per `.orca/reviewers/tests.md`, prefer fakes/real repos over mocks in new tests; use a recording `utils.FakeTelegramApi` (subclass of TelegramApi with placeholder `TelegramConfig(enabled = false, botToken = "test-token", webhookSecret = "test-secret", botName = "test")` and `new DefaultApplicationLifecycle`, as `TelegramApiSpec`/`ParseReceiptActionStatusSpec` already construct it). Never call the real Telegram API.
- `TelegramApiSpec` tests the API via a `FakeRequestHandler` that overrides `client`.
- Test descriptions name the method only ("apply", "editMessage"), never `Type.method`. JSON fixtures are multi-line. All globally-unique values are random (test-isolation reviewer).
- The ProcessDocumentAction classifier gate: a doc with a stored classification uses `documentClassifier.fromStored` (no JEV); a doc without one reads blob bytes (NoOpBlobStorage -> none -> fail-open). `FailingTextractClient` fails if Textract is started, so use a textract cache row for the doc's sha256 to take the cache-hit path.
- Verify with targeted runs only: `sbt "testOnly *SpecName"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Never run the full `sbt test` inside a task.
- Known flake: BackgroundJobTypeRunnerSpec "allowed errors" can race under the full suite. Web tests need Node 24 (irrelevant here, server-only).
